did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, it is said that David was old and advanced in years, and he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
Did you know? The Levites were initially counted from the age of thirty and above, and their total number was 38,000 men.
Did you know? Of the 38,000 Levites, 24,000 were appointed to oversee the work of the house of the Lord, and 6,000 served as officers and judges.
Did you know? 4,000 Levites were assigned to guard the gates, and another 4,000 were musicians appointed to praise the Lord with instruments.
Did you know? David divided the Levites into divisions according to the three main ancestral families: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Did you know? Aaron and his sons were set apart for the priesthood and the sacred service, while the sons of Moses were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
Did you know? After Eleazar died, leaving no sons but only daughters, his daughters married the sons of Kish, their relatives from the family of Merari.
Did you know? The chapter says that the Levites were counted according to their ancestral households, by name and number, for service in the house of the Lord from the age of twenty and above.

Did you know? The reason for the change in the age of service for the Levites was that in David’s time they no longer had to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, because the Lord had given His people rest in Jerusalem.

Did you know? The Levites’ duties included preparing the showbread and grain offerings, managing measures and weights, singing and giving thanks to the Lord morning and evening, and guarding the tent of meeting and the sanctuary.
